documents.content:
1. STATUTORY AUTHORITY AND SCOPE
This policy defines the governance, borrowing privileges, loan durations, overdue fine structures, renewal terms, and loss-of-material liabilities for the Central Library and Learning Resource Centre (DEPT-LIB) housed within the Valmiki Central Library Building at Demo University. These regulations apply equally to all registered undergraduate (UG) students, postgraduate (PG) students, doctoral research scholars, teaching faculty, and administrative staff.

2. SMART CREDENTIALS AND CIRCULATION ELIGIBILITY
2.1 RFID Identification Requirement: Physical access to the library stacks, automated RFID self-checkout kiosks, and manual circulation service counters requires a valid, active Demo University Smart RFID Identity Card issued under POL-ID-CARD and managed via CampusPass (SYS-PASS).
- Entity Disambiguation Note: Student Smart RFID ID Cards (ID under SEC-POL-001 / CampusPass) must not be confused with Instructional Design (ID under ACAD-LMS-005 / LearnSphere LMS).
2.2 Lending Restrictions: Lending, borrowing, or sharing student ID cards to perform proxy book checkouts is strictly prohibited and constitutes a disciplinary infraction referred to the Proctorial Committee (STU-POL-005).

3. BORROWING QUOTAS AND LOAN DURATIONS (POL-LIBRARY)
Borrowing entitlements are partitioned strictly according to academic user categories as registered in UniCampus ERP:
3.1 Undergraduate (UG) Students: Entitled to borrow up to four (4) general circulation books simultaneously for a maximum duration of fourteen (14) calendar days.
3.2 Postgraduate (PG) Students and Doctoral Scholars: Entitled to borrow up to six (6) general circulation books simultaneously for a maximum duration of twenty-eight (28) calendar days.
3.3 Faculty Members: Entitled to borrow up to ten (10) volumes for a standard semester loan period of ninety (90) calendar days.
3.4 Non-Circulating Reference Stacks: Rare manuscripts, encyclopedias, print periodicals, current journal issues, standards, course reserve textbooks, and reference hall materials are strictly non-circulating and cannot be removed from library premises under any circumstances.

4. OVERDUE FINES AND ACCOUNT LOCKOUT THRESHOLDS (PROC-LIB-CIRCULATION)
4.1 Tiered Overdue Fine Structure: Borrowers failing to return circulating materials by the specified due date incur progressive daily penalties:
- Days 1 through 7 of Overdue: Rs. 5 per calendar day per overdue book.
- Day 8 and Onward: Rs. 10 per calendar day per overdue book until the volume is physically checked in at the circulation counter.
4.2 Automated Account Lockout: If a patron accumulates cumulative unpaid library fines exceeding Rs. 50, LibNet (SYS-LIB) automatically applies a borrowing lock to the patron profile. While locked, patrons cannot check out additional books, place online reservation holds, or renew active loans.
4.3 Fine Settlement: Accrued library circulation fines may be settled instantly at the Circulation Counter using integrated PayVarsity POS terminals or online via the LibNet patron portal linked to PayVarsity (SYS-PAY).

5. BOOK LOSS, DAMAGE, AND REPLACEMENT PROTOCOLS
If a borrowed book is lost, stolen, or mutilated, the borrower must immediately notify the Circulation Desk in writing. Borrowers must replace the lost volume with a brand-new copy of the identical or later edition within twenty-one (21) calendar days, accompanied by a non-refundable administrative processing fee of Rs. 100. If the book is out of print or unobtainable, the library assesses recovery charges equivalent to twice the current catalog market value or replacement cost determined by the University Chief Librarian.

6. INSTITUTIONAL NO-DUES CLEARANCE AND INTER-DEPARTMENTAL DEPENDENCIES (REL-006)
Complete clearance of all borrowed books and zero outstanding circulation fine balances in LibNet is mandatory for:
- Generation of Semester End Examination (SEE) hall tickets on ExamShield;
- Semester course registration approvals on UniCampus ERP;
- Formal institutional No-Dues clearance for degree certificate issuance, Transfer Certificate (TC) release, and caution deposit refund under FIN-POL-003 and ACAD-SOP-001.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND INSTITUTIONAL MANDATE
This policy regulates authenticated access to subscription-based digital scholarly resources, licensed electronic journals, bibliographic databases, and remote proxy gateways provisioned by the Central Library and Learning Resource Centre (DEPT-LIB) in partnership with Information Technology Services (DEPT-IT).

2. LICENSED ELECTRONIC SCHOLARLY COLLECTIONS
Demo University subscribes to premier international peer-reviewed research databases to support undergraduate coursework, postgraduate dissertations, and sponsored doctoral research, including:
- IEEE Xplore Digital Library (Electrical, Electronics, and Computer Science);
- ScienceDirect / Elsevier (Engineering, Physical Sciences, Life Sciences);
- ACM Digital Library (Computing Machinery and Software Systems);
- SpringerLink, Scopus, and Web of Science (Multidisciplinary citation databases).

3. ON-CAMPUS AND OFF-CAMPUS AUTHENTICATION MODES
3.1 On-Campus IP Authentication: Users connected to the official university campus enterprise network—either through 802.1X authenticated Wi-Fi (IT-SYS-005) or wired computing laboratory Ethernet ports—receive seamless, automatic IP-authenticated access to all subscribed repositories without secondary login prompts.
3.2 Off-Campus Remote Proxy Gateway: Authorized students, scholars, and faculty accessing resources outside campus premises must authenticate through the LibNet Off-Campus E-Journal Proxy Gateway accessible at: https://libnet.demo.edu.internal/opac. Off-campus access utilizes central Single Sign-On (SSO) credentials linked to the user's active UniCampus ERP account.

4. ACCEPTABLE USE, DATA SECURITY, AND PROHIBITED PRACTICES (IT-POL-001)
Licensed digital resources are governed by statutory copyright laws and publisher licensing agreements. The following conduct is strictly prohibited:
4.1 Prohibition of Automated Scraping: Utilizing automated web scraping scripts, robotic crawlers, batch retrieval bots, offline download managers, or bulk extraction tools to download systematic volumes or entire journal issues is illegal.
4.2 Credential Non-Transferability: User proxy credentials are strictly personal and confidential. Sharing login credentials with unauthorized off-campus acquaintances, commercial entities, or third-party academic networks is a serious breach of IT security.
4.3 Commercial Exploitation: Distributing, selling, or republishing copyrighted content downloaded from university library subscriptions is strictly forbidden.

5. AUDITING, ABUSE DETECTION, AND DISCIPLINARY SANCTIONS
5.1 Automated Anomaly Monitoring: The LibNet proxy server continuously audits traffic patterns. Detection of abnormal spikes in retrieval volume, simultaneous logins from disparate geographic IPs, or bot signatures triggers an immediate automated suspension of the offending user profile.
5.2 Incident Escalation: Suspicious activity generates a Security Incident Report (IR under SEC-SOP-003) transmitted to the Chief Security Officer and Director of IT Infrastructure. Reinstatement requires formal review and disciplinary clearance by the Proctorial Committee (STU-POL-005).
- Entity Disambiguation Note: Security Incident Reports (IR under DEPT-SEC) must not be confused with the Institutional Repository (IR under LIB-POL-004) or the Office of International Relations (IRO-POL-001).

6. TECHNICAL TROUBLESHOOTING AND ASSISTANCE
Patrons encountering proxy authentication timeouts, SSL certificate validation errors, or publisher access blocks should submit a service ticket on ResolveDesk (SYS-RESOLVE) categorized under 'Library Services > E-Resource Proxy Gateway'.

documents.content:
1. PURPOSE AND FACILITY LAYOUT
This document regulates physical access, decorum, noise zoning, opening schedules, and collaborative workspace reservations across the Valmiki Central Library Building, comprising four floors, an 85,000+ print volume repository, dedicated periodicals halls, and specialized digital learning zones.

2. REFERENCE HALL AND PERIODICALS SECTION
2.1 Location and Operating Hours: The Reference Hall and Periodicals Reading Section occupy Floors 1 and 2, operating from 08:00 AM to 10:00 PM on all official working days.
2.2 Strict In-House Consultation: Reference materials—including encyclopedias, dictionaries, statistical yearbooks, current journals, bound archival volumes, and reserved course textbooks—cannot be checked out or removed. Removing reference items from designated halls triggers anti-theft RFID gates and warrants immediate disciplinary referral.
2.3 Non-Disturbance Mandate: Floors 1 and 2 are designated as Absolute Silence Zones. Cell phones must be switched off or placed in silent mode; voice calls, video streaming without headphones, and audible conversations are strictly forbidden.

3. 24/7 NIGHT STUDY HALL AND EXAMINATION OPERATIONS
3.1 Operating Schedule: To support academic preparation during sessional assessments and end-semester finals, the Ground Floor 24/7 Reading Room operates twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a week throughout the academic semester.
3.2 Biometric and RFID Access Security: Entry between 10:00 PM and 06:00 AM is restricted strictly to active students and researchers with valid RFID ID cards verified through CampusPass (SYS-PASS) speed gates at the library entrance.
- Disambiguation Note on Hostel Curfew: Hostel resident students using the 24/7 Reading Room past the standard 10:00 PM curfew must log their night study location via DormTrack (SYS-DORM) in accordance with HSTL-POL-001; random night vigilance checks are conducted jointly by Security and Hostel Wardens.
3.3 Physical Amenities: The 24/7 study zone provides high-speed enterprise Wi-Fi (802.1X), individual carrels with localized power sockets for laptops, ergonomic seating, and filtered drinking water dispensers.

4. DISCUSSION CUBICLE AND GROUP STUDY ROOM BOOKING
4.1 Purpose and Capacity: The library maintains ten (10) soundproof discussion cubicles on Floor 3 for collaborative academic projects, capstone group work, and research team deliberations. Cubicles accommodate groups of 3 to 8 registered students.
- Cross-Domain Disambiguation Note: Library Discussion Cubicles (bookable via LibNet) must not be confused with Academic Conference Rooms (CR under OPS-FAC-003 / Campus Operations) or Student Activity Centre club meeting spaces (SAC-FAC-001).
4.2 Reservation Procedure via LibNet OPAC: Study groups reserve cubicles up to 48 hours in advance through the LibNet portal:
- Minimum Group Size: 3 students (valid student IDs must be entered during booking);
- Maximum Slot Duration: Capped at two (2) continuous hours per group per day to ensure equitable access;
- Check-In Grace Period: The lead applicant must report to the Floor 3 Helpdesk within fifteen (15) minutes of slot commencement; failure to check in releases the cubicle automatically to waitlisted groups.

5. CODE OF CONDUCT AND AMENITIES USAGE
5.1 Consumables Prohibition: Food, snacks, soft drinks, and open beverage containers are strictly prohibited inside all library halls; only spill-proof bottled water is permitted.
5.2 Personal Belongings: Personal textbooks, notebooks, and laptops may be carried inside; personal bags, backpacks, and umbrellas must be deposited at the Ground Floor Property Counter against a brass token.
5.3 Vandalism and Markings: Highlighting, underlining, defacing, or tearing pages from library books or damaging furniture, charging ports, or computing terminals results in a mandatory fine of Rs. 1,000 plus full repair or replacement costs under POL-DISCIPLINE.

documents.content:
1. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE AND MANDATE
This policy establishes the statutory mandate, quality standards, plagiarism verification thresholds, and submission workflows for depositing scholarly intellectual assets into the Demo University Institutional Repository (IR). Managed by the Central Library (DEPT-LIB) through the LibNet Institutional Research Archive module, the repository preserves and disseminates the university's academic scholarship.

2. CONTROLLED POLYSEMY AND ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION (IR)
Within the Demo University enterprise ecosystem, the term 'IR' possesses three distinct, non-overlapping meanings across departments:
2.1 Institutional Repository (IR under DEPT-LIB / LIB-POL-004): The digital research archive preserving faculty publications, master dissertations, and doctoral theses;
2.2 Office of International Relations (IR under DEPT-IRO / IRO-POL-001): The administrative division facilitating student semester exchange programs, foreign dual degrees, and international memoranda of understanding (MOUs);
2.3 Incident Report (IR under DEPT-SEC / SEC-SOP-003): The security documentation protocol logging physical theft, safety infractions, or gate trespassing incidents on campus.

3. MANDATORY DEPOSIT SCOPE AND COVERAGE
Deposit in the Institutional Repository is an absolute prerequisite for degree completion and research sign-off across all academic programs:
3.1 Doctoral Ph.D. Theses: Final approved Ph.D. dissertations submitted under PROG-PHD-ENG and RES-POL-001;
3.2 Master Dissertations: M.Tech dissertation projects (e.g., CSE580 Phase I & II) and MBA master research theses;
3.3 Undergraduate Capstone Projects: Outstanding B.Tech capstone project reports recommended by departmental project evaluation committees;
3.4 Faculty Scholarly Works: Pre-prints, post-prints, conference proceedings, and peer-reviewed journal papers authored by Demo University faculty members.

4. ANTI-PLAGIARISM VERIFICATION AND THRESHOLDS (RES-ETH-001)
Prior to repository archiving, all dissertations and theses must undergo rigorous computerized similarity analysis administered by the Plagiarism & Thesis Verification Unit:
4.1 Authorized Verification Engines: Similarity evaluation is performed exclusively using university-licensed Turnitin / E-Shodh Hub platforms.
4.2 Permissible Similarity Index Ceiling: The overall similarity index must be strictly less than or equal to ten percent (<= 10%), excluding the candidate's own published papers, title pages, formal acknowledgments, and bibliographic references.
4.3 Exclusion Filter Parameters: Quotes enclosed in quotation marks and generic string matches of fourteen (14) words or fewer are automatically excluded.
4.4 Endorsement Slip: Upon confirming similarity <= 10%, the Plagiarism Verification Officer generates a digitally signed Turnitin Verification Certificate and endorsement slip counter-signed by the Research Supervisor.

5. SUBMISSION WORKFLOW AND FILE FORMAT STANDARDS
5.1 Digital Submission Format: Dissertations must be submitted in searchable PDF/A format (ISO 19005 compliant), accompanied by complete metadata (title, abstract, keywords, supervisor name, departmental affiliation, and research grant acknowledgment).
5.2 Upload Protocol via LibNet: The scholar navigates to the LibNet Institutional Research Archive module, enters authenticated ERP credentials, attaches the PDF/A file, and uploads the Turnitin Verification Certificate.
5.3 Library Archival Verification: The Digital Repository In-Charge inspects metadata accuracy within three (3) working days. Once verified, the digital repository receipt is transmitted automatically to UniCampus ERP and the Examination Cell, unblocking oral defense scheduling or graduation clearance.

6. OPEN ACCESS AND EMBARGO PROVISIONS
6.1 Standard Open Access: All archived works are made publicly discoverable via LibNet OPAC under open-access principles.
6.2 Embargo Exceptions: If research findings are subject to an active patent application (RES-IPR-001), commercial sponsorship non-disclosure agreement, or journal publisher embargo, the supervisor and Dean of Research may request an embargo period of six (6) to twelve (12) months. During embargo, descriptive metadata is visible, but full-text access remains restricted to authenticated internal campus IPs.

documents.content:
FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS: CENTRAL LIBRARY AND LEARNING RESOURCE CENTRE

Q1: What are the standard operating hours of the Central Library?
A: General Circulation Stacks, Book Issue Desks, and the Reference Hall operate from 08:00 AM to 10:00 PM on all official working days, and from 09:00 AM to 05:00 PM on Saturdays, Sundays, and notified university holidays. The Ground Floor 24/7 Reading Room remains open round-the-clock, 365 days a year, accessible via RFID card turnstiles (CampusPass).

Q2: What is the borrowing quota and loan duration for undergraduate and postgraduate students?
A: Under POL-LIBRARY:
- Undergraduate (UG) Students: May borrow up to 4 books for 14 calendar days;
- Postgraduate (PG) Students / Research Scholars: May borrow up to 6 books for 28 calendar days;
- Faculty Members: May borrow up to 10 books for 90 days (semester loan).

Q3: What are the overdue fine rates if I return a book late?
A: Overdue fines are calculated automatically by LibNet at Rs. 5 per day per book for the first 7 days of delay, increasing to Rs. 10 per day per book from Day 8 onwards. If your unpaid fine balance exceeds Rs. 50, your library account is automatically locked, preventing further checkouts or renewals.

Q4: What is the Book Bank Scheme and who is eligible to apply?
A: The Book Bank is a specialized social and academic welfare service operated by the Central Library. It provides a complete set of required core engineering and management textbooks for the entire semester to eligible students:
- Category A: Students belonging to SC/ST communities upon verification of category documentation;
- Category B: Economically Weaker Section (EWS) students with verified family annual income below Rs. 2,50,000.
Book Bank sets are issued during the first two weeks of every semester and must be returned within seven (7) days following the completion of Semester End Examinations (SEE).

Q5: Why is my Semester End Exam hall ticket or course registration blocked due to library dues?
A: Under institutional workflow REL-006 and POL-LIBRARY, complete clearance of all library obligations (zero outstanding overdue fines and complete return of circulating volumes) is mandatory. Uncleared fines or unreturned books trigger an automated financial/administrative hold flag in UniCampus ERP, blocking exam hall ticket downloads on ExamShield and preventing online course registration.

Q6: How do I access IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and ACM Digital Library from off-campus?
A: Authenticate through the LibNet Off-Campus E-Journal Proxy Gateway at https://libnet.demo.edu.internal/opac using your standard UniCampus ERP Single Sign-On credentials. Automated crawling or sharing credentials with external parties is strictly prohibited under IT-POL-001.

Q7: What should I do if I lose a borrowed library book?
A: Report the loss immediately to the Circulation Desk to halt the accumulation of daily overdue fines. You must replace the book with a new copy of the same or later edition plus a Rs. 100 processing fee within 21 days. If out of print, you will be assessed replacement costs determined by the University Chief Librarian.

Q8: What is the permissible plagiarism limit for master dissertations and Ph.D. theses?
A: Under RES-ETH-001 and LIB-POL-004, the similarity index measured via Turnitin / E-Shodh Hub must be strictly less than or equal to ten percent (<= 10%), excluding bibliography and quoted phrases of fourteen words or fewer. A certified verification endorsement slip must accompany the digital upload to the Institutional Repository (IR).
